fields.meta_title: Instagram Landing Page Builder for Bio Links | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an Instagram landing page from a prompt. See four examples: a bio link menu, a restock list, salon bookings, and a creator media kit.
fields.h1: Build an Instagram Landing Page for Your Bio, Stories and Reels
fields.hero_description: Build an Instagram landing page that turns taps from a profile, Story or Reel into rows in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sits Behind the Link in Your Bio
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page a tap from Instagram lands on, and everything that happens to the visitor's answers after it.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt, one page per post

Describe the page in a sentence and Emergent builds it: the headline, the buttons, the form, and the table behind them. Rename a button or add a field later with another prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every tap saved with its button

The app saves each tap and each signup to a database you own, with the button name and the time. Sort the rows by week to see which post sent people to the page, and which did not.
fields.feature_3:
Forms that fit a thumb

Emergent can build the form as one question per screen, so a visitor who arrives from a Story answers on a phone, one tap at a time. The last screen asks for the email address.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a visitor needs a person

Set a rule in the prompt, such as a booking request for a Saturday, and the app sends an email or Slack alert to the person who handles it, with the visitor's answers in the message.
fields.feature_5:
Signups passed to the tools you use

The app connects to any tool with an API, so new subscribers can go to your email platform and new leads to HubSpot. Data syncs in and out, and the page keeps a copy of each row.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain in the bio, your code in a repo

Publish the page on your own domain (custom domains use credits) and put that address in your bio. On paid plans, export the code to your GitHub repository and keep working on it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every button on the bio page counts its own taps

Ferngrove Pottery keeps four buttons on the page its Instagram bio links to: the mug drop, workshop dates, the newsletter, and wholesale. Each tap is saved as a row with the button's name. Of last week's 1,240 taps, the mug drop took 620 and workshop dates 370, with 160 for the newsletter and 90 for wholesale.
fields.tab_content_2:
318 viewers want the candle back in stock

A sold-out candle gets its own Reel at Saltmarsh Candle Co., and a Story with a link sticker sends viewers to a restock page for the Low Tide candle. The page asks for one thing, an email address. In 3 days, 318 viewers signed up. When the owner marks Low Tide back in stock, the app emails all 318.
fields.tab_content_3:
A Saturday color request reaches its stylist

Clients tap the link in Juniper Vale Studio's bio and land on a booking request form that asks for a service and a day. A color request for a Saturday goes to Mara Okonjo, who takes the studio's Saturday color clients, as an email with the client's answers. Every request is saved to the bookings table, whoever it goes to.
fields.tab_content_4:
The manager sees every budget of $2,000 or more

Brands that find Wren Halloway, a food creator, through her bio land on her media kit: her audience numbers and an inquiry form. An inquiry with a budget of $2,000 or more, such as Brightloaf Bakery's $3,500 offer, is emailed straight to her manager, Dario Pelt. Smaller budgets wait in a list Wren reads on Fridays.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Instagram Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take an Instagram landing page from one post's goal to a tagged, tested page your bio and Stories can link to.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what one tap should do
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Plan the page for a phone
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tag every link before you post it
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one job for the page, such as a restock signup or a booking request. A visitor who taps through from a Story has seen one post. Give the page one headline and one action that match it, and leave the rest of the catalog for other pages.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A tap from a Story opens on the phone it was read on. Keep the headline to one line, put the action near the top, and ask only for what the next step needs. An email address is enough for a restock list.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent the page's job, the fields, and what happens after someone submits it, including who gets an alert and which table keeps the entry. Emergent builds the page and its database from that prompt, and another prompt changes either one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign to each link, with its own campaign value for the bio, each Story, and each Reel. Google Analytics says to use all three whenever you add parameters to a URL. Then each signup traces back to one post.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write the routing rules in plain words
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name who handles which answer: a wholesale inquiry goes to the owner, a same-week booking goes to the front desk. The app sends that person an email or Slack alert, and every entry is still kept in your own table for later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it from your own profile
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the published page on a phone from your own profile, tap every button, and submit a test entry. Check that the row is in the table and the alert reached the right person before the link goes anywhere public.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put the link where people tap
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the page's address to your bio, and to Stories with Instagram's Link sticker, which adds a link to a Story. Point each Reel's caption to the bio. Once a week, compare entries by campaign value and retire the posts that send nobody.

faq_plan.q: What is an instagram landing page?
faq_plan.a: An Instagram landing page is the web page someone reaches after tapping a link on Instagram, from a bio, a Story, or an ad. It is built for that one visitor: one offer, one action, and a form or button sized for a phone screen.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an instagram landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page in a prompt, such as a restock list for a sold-out product, and Emergent's AI landing page builder writes the page, the form, and the database behind it. Publish it, put the address in your bio, and tap through it on your own phone before you post.

faq_plan.q: What do good Instagram landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: They match the post that sent the visitor, and they ask for one thing. Each one carries the same photo and words as that post, one action, the detail that action depends on (a price, a date, a size), and a line that says what happens after the tap. The restock page above opens on the same Low Tide candle its Story showed.

faq_plan.q: Does an Instagram landing page need SEO?
faq_plan.a: Not for the visitors Instagram sends, because they arrive by tapping a link, not by searching. It is worth the work when the same page should also be found in search, such as a booking page for a salon in your town. Then give the page a title and a description that say what it offers, and follow the rest of the landing page seo basics.

faq_plan.q: Should every post get its own Instagram landing page?
faq_plan.a: No. Give a page to each offer, not to each post. Five Reels about the same candle restock can share one restock page. Give each link its own campaign value and you still see which Reel sent the signups. Build a new page when the offer changes, such as a new workshop date or a new product.

faq_plan.q: How do I know which Instagram landing pages are working best?
faq_plan.a: Divide signups by taps for each campaign value, and compare the rates once a week. Your own counts decide which pages work best, not a design you admire. When one Reel sends plenty of taps and few signups while another converts well, look at what the first Reel promised and whether the page shows it. Then fix the headline or stop linking that post.

faq_plan.q: Can I use an Instagram landing page for a product launch?
faq_plan.a: You can run a launch in two stages. Before launch day, the page collects email addresses from people who tap through from your teaser Reels. On launch day, change the headline and the button to the order link, and email the list once. Treat it like any campaign landing page with an end date: when the launch is over, point your bio at the next page and keep the list.

faq_plan.q: Can I change an Instagram landing page after the link is live?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent changes the page when you prompt it again: ask for a new headline for this week's Reel, or one more field on the form. Publish it, then open it from your own profile to check it before the next post goes up. Change one thing at a time. The weekly counts then show what that change did.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after someone signs up on an Instagram landing page?
faq_plan.a: Show a confirmation screen that says what happens next and when, such as a line that the visitor will get an email when the candle is back in stock. Then add a button back to your profile, and the visitor can keep scrolling your posts instead of closing the tab. Put both in the prompt, and Emergent builds them with the page.

faq_plan.q: Can I send Instagram ad traffic to an Instagram landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each ad its own page, or at least its own campaign value, and count signups against what each ad cost. The same rules as any ppc landing page apply: the headline repeats the ad's offer, the page asks for one action, and no menu leads the visitor away from it.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this keyword mixes Instagram's own pages, a builder homepage and example galleries; none shows what happens after the tap from a bio, a Story or a Reel. This page shows four Instagram landing pages built from a prompt and follows each tap to where it lands: a link-in-bio page that counts taps per button, a restock list fed by a Story link sticker, a salon booking request sent to the right stylist, and a creator's media kit that routes brand inquiries by budget. The FAQ covers the definition, what the page should hold, link-in-bio pages versus landing pages, tagging links to see which post drove a signup, search indexing, and one page per campaign or ad.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: "Ferngrove Pottery keeps four buttons...", "A sold-out candle gets its own Reel...", "Describe the page in a sentence and Emergent builds it".

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail ("Of last week's 1,240 taps, the mug drop took 620", "Smaller budgets wait in a list Wren reads on Fridays"); no AI tells; one imprecise "sort by post" phrasing recorded as a note.

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in headings (link in bio landing page, tiktok, youtube, facebook ads); scope spans bio, Stories, Reels and ads, so it does not take the link-in-bio page's keyword; FAQ links ppc, campaign and SEO siblings by their own anchors.
